newsitem.title: USA: CCC seeks 32,380 tonnes grains to ship to N. Korea.
newsitem.headline: CCC seeks 32,380 tonnes grains to ship to N. Korea.

text.p: The Commodity Credit Corp of the U.S. Department of Agriculture said it was seeking a total of 32,380 tonnes of U.S. corn, rice and corn/soy blend for shipment to North Korea.
The grain was to be delivered to U.S. port before April 1. Offers were due on February 25.
The deal included 5,000 tonnes of corn-soy blend, 20,780 tonnes of yellow corn and 6,600 tonnes milled rice.
The United States on Wednesday formally announced an extra $10 million in food aid for North Korea, considerably more than originally expected and above last year's donation of $6.4 million.
But the aid, amounting to about 100,000 tons of commodities, still falls far short of internationally recognized needs, judged by agencies to be upwards of 2.3 million tons of commodities.
The United States has chosen the World Food Program as the channel for the aid.
In June 1996, the CCC had also issued a special invitation for 13,100 tonnes of grains to North Korea, the CCC said.
"We purchased 3,000 tonnes of cornmeal, 3,500 tonnes of corn/soy blend and 6,600 tonnes of milled rice for donation to North Korea," a CCC official said.
